title: Bin El Ouidane reservoir, 16 Jul to 14 Sep 2026
summary: From 16 Jul to 14 Sep 2026 the radar shows the lake shrinking from 33.83 km2 to 30.17 km2, or -10.8%. Because 17.1% of the 16 Jul outline falls on land in the optical photo, this loss may be overstated.

sections.heading: What changed
sections.text: Over 60 days the lake changed by -3.66 km2. Mean HV moved by -0.03 dB and mean HH rose by 0.42 dB. In HH, 1.99 km2 turned brighter by more than 3 dB and 0.34 km2 darker; in HV, 0.62 km2 turned brighter and 0.45 km2 darker.

sections.heading: Where, by terrain type
sections.text: The open water type darkened by 0.38 dB in HH. Rough dry ground and fields had 0.77 km2 brighter in HH, rising 0.47 dB. The changing fields type rose 1.07 dB in HV and 1.24 dB in HH, and built-up land rose 0.35 dB in HH.

sections.heading: Possible causes
sections.text: Possible cause: shadowed slopes joined to the lake mask on 16 Jul; the outlines on the map would show it. Possible cause: real summer drawdown; the dam's level record would confirm it. Possible cause for the changing fields: crops growing on a few plots; a field visit would check it.

sections.heading: Limits
sections.text: Neither date carries a flag, but the 16 Jul lake figure deserves care. NASA has no NISAR data from 27 Jul to 10 Aug 2026, so nothing between 16 Jul and 21 Aug 2026 is seen. Lake areas are approximate: 17.1% and 9.7% of the outline falls on land in the optical photo.

sections.heading: What an agency could do next
sections.text: Confirm the 3.66 km2 loss with the dam's level record before reporting it. Visit the changing fields to learn which crops raise HV in this season.
